Subject: Recap from today — volume profile + $/1M token ask

Hi Liam — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap and two asks so we can pull together a clean price comparison versus the public hosts (OpenAI, Anthropic) and a recommended Redwood band.

Call recap (5 min):
- HealthSync expects peak traffic from clinical summarization feature (inbound PDFs -> 1–3k tokens per doc) and an assistant flow for clinicians (short prompts ~150 tokens).
- Target pilot: 50k MAU, estimated 15M tokens/month initially, up to 45M in steady state (12–18 month runway).
- Compliance: must keep PHI within your VPC for production; pilot ok with redacted test data.

What we need from you (asks):
1) Confirm ballpark budget range for inference per month (USD) or target $/1M tokens. If you have internal target unit economics that simplifies the recommender.
2) Any existing host contracts or target comparisons you want us to include (e.g., specific OpenAI plan, Anthropic pricing, or internal on-prem numbers).

Our deliverable: 1-page competitive rate parity grid ($/1M tokens for relevant model classes + recommended Redwood offering: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and an ops note on how batching/quantization and caching could move the unit price. We’ll attach the forecast template for you to validate.

Next steps: if you confirm budget band and share the forecast (or let us fill it), we’ll return a side-by-side $/1M comparison and a recommended pilot pricing by EOD Friday PST.

Cheers,
Mateo
Lead Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Recap from today — volume profile + $/1M token ask

Thanks Mateo — appreciate the clear recap. Quick answers below.

1) Budget: for pilot (first 3 months) we have an internal budget of $8k–$12k / month. For production we’re modeling $30k–$50k / month depending on uptake. On a unit basis our finance lead suggested a target of $7–$12 per 1M tokens to be competitive against our current AWS-hosted baseline.

2) Comparison targets: please include latest OpenAI pay-as-you-go public rates (text-gen family) and Anthropic Scale API list prices. We don’t have an incumbent contract with OpenAI or Anthropic yet — we run smaller experiments on an internal GPU instance at ~ $18 / 1M effective due to low utilization.

Notes: we are PHI-sensitive and will likely need Private deployment for production, but pilot can run on Hosted with strict logging disabled/pseudonymized.

I’ve attached a short procurement intake and the usage forecast we discussed.

—Liam

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 11 Mar 2027 14:07:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: HealthSync volume/budget — initial rate parity sketch

Folks — forwarding Liam’s reply. I pulled together an initial parity grid and a few bullet recommendations. See attached host_comparison_grid.csv. Highlights:

- Baseline public host list pricing (as of Mar 2027):
  - OpenAI (text-gen family): ~$16–22 / 1M tokens depending on model and context window when amortized.
  - Anthropic (Claude-like): ~$18–25 / 1M tokens across small/medium/large families.
  - Common open-hosts (managed Llama/Meta variants): ~$8–15 / 1M depending on batching and quantization.

- Redwood positioning:
  - Hosted (managed): For pilot, we can target $10–14 / 1M with batching suggestions and shared caches — fits Liam’s pilot budget at the upper end.
  - Dedicated (reserved GPU pool): With a 12-month commit and 2–3x pilot scale, we can get to $6–9 / 1M by tuning batch sizes, using int8 kernels, and enabling prefix cache for the clinician assistant flow.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): Higher fixed cost but best for PHI; unit economics depend on customer infra. For HealthSync, we should model both hosted pilot and a private production path.

Actionable asks from us to make the numbers precise:
- Confirm target model class (lightweight open model for summaries vs larger safety-checked model for triage) — this changes token efficiency 12–20%.
- Confirm 3, 6, 12 month expected token ramp (Liam’s numbers helpful; we’ll push back if contrived).

I’m proposing we present two pricing paths to HealthSync: Pilot Hosted (30–60 day commit, canopy pricing) and Production Dedicated (12-month commit, lower $/1M). I’ll annotate the grid with conservative and aggressive assumptions.

Ben
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
